source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Collect all relevant inspection reports and documents including permits, certifications, and previous audit findings. Make sure to note the date, time, and details of the inspection conducted.

3. Briefly describe the purpose of the fire-safety check.
Outline the objective of the fire safety inspection to place the failures in context, for example, to ensure compliance with local fire codes and regulations, confirm the effectiveness of installed fire protections systems, and protect the safety of inhabitants or occupants.

4. List the exact observations made during the inspection.
Provide a detailed and specific account of what was observed during the inspection. This should include any non-functioning or missing fire safety equipment (such as extinguishers, sprinklers, alarms, fire doors, emergency lighting, signage, etc.), blocked or inadequate emergency exits, any unsafe practices observed (e.g., disabling fire alarm systems), and any other hazards or code breaches.

5. Record the reasons for failure.
Document why the specific items
